en.name: Toribio de Mogrovejo
en.summary: Spanish layman sent to Peru as Archbishop of Lima, who traveled the vast diocese tirelessly and confirmed both Rose of Lima and Martin de Porres.
en.body: Toribio de Mogrovejo was a Spanish lawyer and layman, not even ordained, when King Philip II unexpectedly appointed him Archbishop of Lima in the recently colonized viceroyalty of Peru, requiring his rapid ordination before he departed for the New World in 1581. Once in Peru he undertook exhausting missionary journeys across the vast and difficult terrain of his archdiocese, reportedly traveling on foot or muleback for years at a time, learning local indigenous languages, and holding regional councils that established lasting norms for evangelization and clergy conduct in Spanish America. He was a fierce defender of the rights of indigenous peoples against the abuses of colonial encomienda landholders, and personally administered the sacraments to enormous numbers of people, including confirming both the young Rose of Lima and Martin de Porres. He died in 1606 while still traveling his diocese and was canonized in 1726.
